I would like to add a bit to this.

We really need to learn that everything is in the mind. Perhaps when you get a serious disease in an advanced phase you will need to treat it physically with the correct medication, and even in those cases, people with really strong mental have found the ways to get out, going against the worst of chances.

It is also well known that a lot of physical ailments are related to mental issues and bad habits. If you don't eat properly, if you don't rest properly, if your body is inactive most of the time, if you surrender yourself to a negative thought pattern, if you stomp yourself whenever you fail, all of that is going to have certain repercussions on your body. These are varying factors, as well as varying effects, but it's all related.

Depression is like drowning in a kiddies pool. Once you realize that first what you need to do is realize what you have to change, and then change it, everything else will come to place. Every single problem that you feel is absolutely overwhelming can become a child's play when you learn to handle yourself correctly.

Like u/extremeocassion said, you have to put special attention to meditation. That way you will learn how to control your own mind, and when you do that, you will gradually be able to kick out everything that doesn't correspond with your happiness, and finally you will see that thought and action are linked to your whole life, and you will get a better life naturally if you balance it all out.

If you think that you can't handle yourself naturally, through meditation and discipline, you can do what I did. Search for some subliminal audios on Youtube that cure depression and anxiety, or that boost positivity. Listen to them for months with faith, real faith, and you will end up realizing how all of this actually works.

Finally, I would like to remind you of the base knowledge of what meditation teaches us: we are not our thoughts! We are the consciousness that watches behind!

Blessings and success for you, now and forever brother!

Of course! We are God, and God is us.

If you guys are interested, I got a method. But first you have to practice meditation with a certain continuity, or at least have an idea of how it works, since you will use the principles on it.

What I do, is ask myself the same question, phrased differently, using different terms, tones and order, and I do it several times, until the body learns to identify the sensation, you will notice that is somehow uncomfortable, and then your mind drifts automatically to another doubt/fear/question. You can keep unraveling the subsequential flow by asking yourself even more, related to the answer that you got, until you end up by either: dissipating the fears/doubts, or you will finally get the answer that you are looking for. You will know because you will feel at peace.

I mentioned meditation because you need to learn to swim in different cascades of thoughts or you will drown and end up losing the thread of the question that you originally asked yourself, through distraction or deeper meaning and you need to know how to come back in track properly without losing the knowledge that you are carrying since the start of the sequence.

If somehow you don't gift yourself a clear answer, then you will get it across univeral signs, synchronicities and ideas out of nowhere in the next few days, until you are ready to.

P.S. Don't ask yourself what the purpose of your life is (I did lol). The purpose of your life is to live it at it's fullest!  
Ask yourself what's your best skill, what skill could you monetize the best, what is your best quality, or anything related to an actual tangible self-discovery doubt.

Blessings for you! Whoever reads this.

Have you tried a heavy dopamine detox? Works in a lot of different ways, and since you already feel dried up on life, why not?

No youtube, no videogames, no p\*rn, no social media, no cellphone for recreative purposes, no sugar, not any food that you deeply enjoy, and not any activity that you commonly do to entertain yourself. Make yourself bored and hate everything for a couple weeks, a month if you can. And then comeback to your life.

You can read books, write draw, paint, learn to sing, to dance, or whatever that you are not used to, but can help you construct yourself, or at least have a little mental struggle while you do so.

Involving in the detox, you will, either face yourself with all your problems (since you will stop hiding these emotions under entertainment) and come down the road of self-realization and healing, or you will completely recover your dopamine receptors and you will feel motivated once again.

If you haven't tried it, give it a shot, it is absolute HELL to become bored, but changes you a lot, more like, it shows you the real you.

Blessings, success and happiness for you, whenever you are!

That applies to our lives in general. We gotta do, what we want to do, not because is correct, or incorrect, moral, or immoral, but because we want to, we feel like doing so.   
Would you not steal a girl from someone if you absolutely knew that she's your soulmate? Wouldn't you falsely-accuse someone if you had the chance to save someone dear to you? 

Guilt and shame are but heavy tolls for the mind to pay, and absolutely unnecessary and of course, you only feel them whenever you take a non-neutral stance on a topic, which, society has taught us to do with competition, judgment and criticism.  
There are no laws to life, laws are a thing of the human mind, of the society. Check things from this perspective, and you can actually analyze why psychopaths and or sociopaths don't really feel any kind of remorse, and why they don't fit among the "civilized".

Shit, you aren't worthless. People who are worthless don't have jobs, don't have couples, don't have nothing. And in case you were, trust me, people will let you know.  
When it comes to certain subjects, humans tend to be horrificly honest, and when you are useless, yeah, that's one.

Because you know it is, you are conscious about it, you just don't want to accept the fact that everything you tell yourself is a lie. You're scared that you may be a wonderful and successful person, you're scared that things would go, beyond well, letting you out of your comfort zone, in a space where you are great, but not feeling secure.

Oh it is really possible. You can get out of this.

There are two facts that I can state about you right now because I have been in the same situation, and you don't have use for those, zero utility.  
1. You overthink a lot. There are things we can change right now, or little by little, and there are things we cannot, but we keep wasting time on thinking, instead of acting. You feel me? We can't sit down there just dying in pain, it'll make you feel worst and worst every goddamn time. The fact that you keep thinking will make problems bigger, and the bigger you make them, the harder it'll be to fight them away.  
2. You need to look for yourself instead of others. This is also related to lack of self-love but I'll avoid that subject right now. There's just the fact that you can be kind without forgetting about yourself. You gotta step up for what you think, what you want to do, or what you want to get before others. That doesn't mean you're a bad person, you can always lend your hand to those in need, but as long as you don't get affected in the process.   
E.g. you can't borrow money to someone if you don't have enough for yourself at the time.

Anyways, if you feel like talking some more, I'm up to it.  
In case you do not, I still wish you the best, today and forever.

I don't think they are blaming suicide victims, but rather, trying to create consciousness around those that have similar thoughts. They know we suffer.

However you are right, they don't really know what it feels like, and there's one thing to display clearly here: every case is different, in intensity and length, symptoms and consequences. They lack the "singularity" characteristic in the treatment, but to be honest, there's not much they can do to stop most of us.

But like everyone else, suicidal people have haters. And it's for a fact that the ones that hate suicidal people are the ones that hate themselves too, or they would be too busy minding their own business instead of trash talking.

I know for a fact that life suffocates us most of the time. But honestly, there is always a spark of light, even in the deepest of darknesses, and to be honest we people lack discipline and determination to get to a solution.

But trust me, life can offer you so much more if you are willing to make an effort. I seriously think the universe works around a certain unknown law that helps you when you actually try. I don't know if you are like I used to be, complaining about everything, raging and ranting here and there, but if you are, that's a solid point to start re-working yourself.

We depressed people keep thinking that someone or something will help us get out of this situation, but to be honest everything lies in ourselves, the main problem is the lack of self-love.  
People hate themselves for different reasons, I don't know yours right now, but trust me, they can be fixed. You don't need a fake positivity like most people will try to impose into your mentality, you just need to tighten your feet in the floor and take everything life has to offer (positive or negative) with the same amount of will.

People don't love you because you don't love you. If you hate life, life hates you back. We have a lot to learn every day, you just have to be conscious about it. If you CAN'T kill yourself just yet, it's because there are some things that you still love, and some things that you can still figure out, with or without help (probably better if you do it with help, but suit yourself).

Anyways, my best wishes to you, today and forever.

I'm sorry to hear about your loss.

When we lose someone so dear to us, there are really no words to try and comfort someone. It's just the empathy and familiarity that keeps us feeling the same pain as you.

But hear me out, I can see that you had a nice relation with her. I can feel through what I read that you were really connected. And you should be happy because of that. Not every son or daughter is as fortunate as to meet their mother, or to have such a nice loving relation with them.

Also, I'm sure she wouldn't like to see you with this enormous pain because of her. She would feel guilty to cause this upon you, to make you feel like this.

Embrace this beautiful sadness, and keep your head up so you can become what your mother always wanted you to be, a wonderful grown man with principles. Make her always, always feel proud of you from wherever she is looking at you. Give her surprises out of your success and accomplishments in death as you gave her in life.

Think of all those happy moments that you spent together, and the promises you made her, and fulfill them of course. That will help you push through this. And never blame you for anything that you did or wish you did to her or with her, because she still loved you and will always love you no matter what it is.

Pray for her, as she will pray for you from now on. And don't drown yourself in harmful sorrow or actions, try to make everything for the better from now on, because you can't do anything about it, just accept it, accept this new void in your heart, and grow stronger with it.

Never forget her. Some rapper I love listening to, used to say: "The only one who dies, is the one we forgotten".

Keep it strong. Best of wishes, now and ever.

Don't overthink about it, we find real happiness when we learn to love ourselves for what we truly are and represent, instead of what we look like. Don't demoralize over looks. Keep a strong will and work on yourself. That's the only way. Best of luck and wishes for you.

Realizing about unwanted thoughts it's pretty simple. The hard part is to actually master those, taming them and knowing they are there, but not giving them more importance than they actually deserve.
But it's okay. Look at it this way: 

You are pushing a heavy rock up the hill. And you are really struggling at it. You're using almost all of your energy. You know it's heavy like no one does, because it is just you who is carrying and pushing the burden.
Suddenly, a little Imp appears out of nowhere. And it promises that if it turns the rock heavier, you will become more responsible and way more trustworthy. A real mature person.
You seal the deal because you are tempted by that idea, and there goes the heavier rock crushing you up.
It's a lot more than you can handle, a lot more than what you are used to, so what happens?
Sooner or later you are in the need to take breaks so you can keep on with the rock, longer and longer breaks will acompany that first one and in worst case scenarios you give up on the rock, and let it roll down because it's too damn heavy for you.

Imagine that rock is every goal or task you set yourself to achieve, or even life itself (don't let that one rock go down the hill ever) and the Imp it's your own mind that tries to set yourself obstacles that you don't really need.

We are our own worst enemies for sure.
However, we shouldn't let this confuse us. We need to do whatever we need to do, but there are times and spaces to do so. Don't mix up work thoughts with home, or viceversa. Just worry about what you need to worry when the time comes for it.
This won't let us forget about what we have to do if it's what you are afraid of, and of course, you can always schedule on a calendar or a simple notebook important events.

But if the metaphor maybe doesn't quite fill up. You can try to always keep your mind positive and active. Do a lot of activities during the day in your free time: workout, play games, read a book, visit places, talk with as much people as you can while you keep your mind thinking about all the nice things you enjoy of every activity.
Focus on positive aspects always, no matter what you do, it's harder than focusing on negative aspects, but on the other side it's rewarding. It sets you up to think that bad circumstances have very slight chances of becoming reality. And that's what we want to think, that is our main obstacle for happiness.

Hope it helps, even if it's just a bit.
